There are two different meanings of top secret. One is that something is a secret in the normal meaning of the word (top merely indicating importance). The other is a formal designation covered by the clissified information rules. What she did was divulge something that is designated as Top Secret under the rules, but is not actually a secret anymore because it has already been publicly disclosed. Note, that just because information is no longer secret (small s) does not remove the information from being covered by the rules governing classified information and so the information may still be Top Secret (big S).

If you are subject to the terms of the agreement one must sign to have access to classified material, you are bound by them regardless of whether the information otherwise becomes public or not. So even though the information was already publicly known, she should not have shared it. Almost no one ever gets in trouble for this. At most they get told not to do it again.
